summary: Initial discovery with Auriga Labs about migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated (or Private). Key drivers: cost predictability, latency control, data residency and compliance. Customer wants eval parity with current OpenAI/Anthropic flows and clarity on vLLM/TGI compatibility. Agreed to run a POC with their prompt set and a throughput/latency benchmark. Security docs + pricing to be shared.
topics: Current stack: OpenAI hosted (usage spikes, rate limits)
Need for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private
Evaluation plan and metrics (latency, 99th pct, cost per 1k tokens)
Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript:
[15:30] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining—I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account.
[15:31] Ben Carter: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Ben, CTO at Auriga Labs. We run most of our prod inference against OpenAI and a few Anthropic endpoints for chat stuff, but costs are spiking and latency jitter is killing some of our synchronous flows.
[15:32] Maya Patel: Understood. Diego and Aria from our solutions team are here to dig into performance and the POC. Quick ask: what are your main decision criteria?
[15:33] Saira Malik: Parity first: we need outputs to match our current evals. Also predictable pricing—right now bursts blow past our budgets. Security is also a blocker; we need SOC 2 and KMS, plus VPC options.
[15:33] Diego Ramos: On parity—are you using any custom fine-tuning, or mostly prompt engineering against OpenAI models?
[15:34] Saira Malik: Mostly prompt engineering. A couple of models are fine-tuned through OpenAI but small. More important is that the latency and tokenization differences don't change the top answers on our customer-critical prompts.
[15:35] Evan Long: And infra-wise, we need predictable throughput during peak batch windows. We currently hit bursts 3x/week.
[15:35] Aria Chen: OK, good signal. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so peak throughput is far more predictable vs pay-as-you-go. There's also our Private option if you require a VPC/private control plane.
[15:36] Ben Carter: How compatible is Redwood with vLLM and TGI? Our infra folks have some homegrown TGI-based endpoints already.
[15:36] Diego Ramos: Redwood's runtime supports models commonly deployed via vLLM/TGI; we provide a model catalog and compatibility mappings. That said, small differences can occur due to kernel selection, quantization, and attention optimizations. We typically run eval parity tests using your prompt set.
[15:37] Saira Malik: Are there known failure modes? Like different tokenization causing hallucinations or different stop behavior?
[15:38] Diego Ramos: Occasionally tokenization and temperature semantics differ slightly; in practice our teams tune decoding settings to match. For example, we adjust top-p/top-k and logits bias mapping and can export tokenization reports. We'll include a mapping doc in the POC.
[15:39] Priya Rao: On security, do you support customer-managed KMS? We need keys never leaving our control.
[15:39] Aria Chen: Yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and for Dedicated we offer a KMS integration pattern—I'll share our KMS whitepaper. We also have audit logs, RBAC and SAML SSO.
[15:40] Ben Carter: What's the typical latency numbers? We're trying to keep p95 under 120ms for single-turn completions (approx 512 tokens max).
[15:40] Diego Ramos: On comparable GPUs and sequence lengths we often see similar or better p95 than OpenAI for short completions when using optimized kernels and prefix KV caching. For 512 tokens, p95 depends on batching policy—if you need strict low-latency we recommend smaller shard pools and disable large batching, but that increases cost. We'll propose trade-offs in the POC.
[15:41] Evan Long: Cost trade-off sounds similar to what we face now. How does Dedicated pricing compare? We have monthly predictable load but variable spikes.
[15:42] Maya Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity. You commit to a pool size which gives much lower unit cost and stable throughput. We also have burst options to handle spikes. I'll send pricing scenarios based on your typical qps and token volume.
[15:42] Saira Malik: For the eval parity, will you run our prompts against both OpenAI and Redwood variants and provide diffs?
[15:43] Diego Ramos: Yes, we'll run side-by-side evals: identical seeds where applicable, token-level outputs, and quality metrics (exact match, rouge, embedding similarity). We'll also capture latency, cost-per-1k tokens and energy per request if useful.
[15:44] Ben Carter: Network-wise, our security team will want VPC peering and restricted egress. Can Redwood handle that for Dedicated?
[15:44] Aria Chen: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; for Private deployments we can run inside your VPC entirely. We'll ask for a list of allowed IPs and routing requirements—Evan, can you gather those?
[15:45] Evan Long: Yep, I'll get the network constraints and whether we need flow logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[15:46] Priya Rao: Also need retention policies and support for audit log export (splunk/elastic). Are logs PII redacted by default?
[15:46] Aria Chen: We can configure log retention and export. For sensitive data we offer options to disable logging of user content or mask PII pre-ingest. We'll include our default retention and masking settings in the security pack.
[15:47] Ben Carter: Timelines—if we like the POC, how long to stand up Dedicated?
[15:47] Maya Patel: From signed commitment to live typically 4–6 weeks for Dedicated (depending on config). Private (VPC/on-prem) can be longer if there's heavy network or compliance gatekeeping.
[15:48] Saira Malik: One more thing: we use TGI locally for some models; we'd like to reuse artifact compatibility. Can you run our TGI checkpoints or do we need conversion?
[15:48] Diego Ramos: We can support many TGI/vLLM checkpoints; sometimes conversion or re-quantization is needed for optimal perf. We'll validate your artifacts during the POC and note any conversion steps.
[15:49] Priya Rao: Regarding compliance, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence?
[15:50] Aria Chen: Yes, SOC 2 and ISO certificates are available; I'll attach the certs and the scope matrix. We'll also share our standard contract language for data residency and breach notification.
[15:50] Ben Carter: Great. Any pitfalls we should be aware of when migrating from OpenAI endpoints?
[15:51] Diego Ramos: Expect some small diffs due to tokenization/decoder semantics. Also watch for throughput tuning—moving from fully managed to Dedicated gives you control but adds configuration decisions (batching, cache sizes, quantization profile). We'll help with suggested profiles based on your workload.
[15:52] Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood to send pricing, security pack, KMS notes; Auriga to send eval prompts and network constraints. POC to be scheduled next week for a 1-week run. Diego will design benchmark harness.
[15:53] Ben Carter: Sounds good. Let's aim to have the POC kickoff on Monday if possible.
[15:54] Maya Patel: Perfect. We'll follow up with a calendar invite and the materials. Thanks everyone.
[15:55] End of recording.
